blocks.title: The Water Cycle
blocks.subtitle: How water moves between oceans, air, and land

blocks.text: The Sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers. Liquid water turns into invisible water vapour and rises into the air. Plants also release vapour through their leaves, which is called transpiration.
As water vapour rises, it cools. Cooled vapour changes back into tiny liquid droplets around dust particles. Billions of these droplets gather to form clouds.
When cloud droplets grow heavy, they fall as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This water runs into rivers, soaks into the ground, or fills lakes and oceans, and the cycle begins again.

blocks.title: Worked example: rain on a roof
blocks.body:
How much water does a 20 mm rainfall deliver to a roof with an area of 50 m²?

One millimetre of rain over one square metre equals exactly 1 litre of water.
blocks.code:
Rain per m² = 20 mm x 1 L = 20 L
Total water = 20 L x 50 m² = 1000 L
blocks.takeaway: That roof collects about 1000 litres, or 1 cubic metre, of water.

questions.question: What drives evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy warms liquid water until it becomes vapour.

questions.question: What happens during condensation?
options: Water vapour cools into liquid droplets
questions.explanation: Cooling vapour changes into liquid droplets, which form clouds.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail.
